text:
rachel: Heads-up: onboarding sample for function-calling + json_mode is flaky. Repro in local and in a customer sandbox. Errors only when auth refresh triggers a retry mid-stream.

priya: can you drop the smallest failing log? streaming + schema validation timing bugs are usually subtle.

rachel: minimal trace:
```
POST /v1/chat.generate {model: 'rw-4-large', json_mode: true, function_call: true}
<< stream chunk 1 >> '\n{"result": [{"user": {"id": "u1", "name": "A'
SDK (js): Ajv.validate(...) -> throws JSONError: unexpected token at 1
<< stream chunk 2 >> 'lice"}}], "meta": {...}}'
```
This happens after the SDK did an auth refresh and retried the request. The validator tried to validate mid-stream and saw a concatenated buffer.

tom: I saw this last week. JS SDK's stream validator runs on each data event. If the retry layer replays and we append to the same buffer we can end up with two half-docs glued together that look like valid JSON to the parser but not to schema.

manuel: py-sdk behavior differs: we accumulate until EOF (or a final marker) then pydantic validates. That explains parity complaints from docs and customers.

priya: reproduction I used (node):
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({auth: {refresh: true}});
await client.chat.generate({json_mode:true, stream:true, function_call:true});
// trigger token refresh while stream in-flight
```
I can repro consistently when refresh happens ~150-400ms into the stream.

rachel: proposed short-term options:
- JS: add conservative guard in stream validator: only run Ajv when braces/brackets balanced OR on an explicit final chunk.
- SDK infra: include an `x-rw-final-chunk: 1` header for streamed json responses so clients know it's complete.
- Retry layer: make retries produce new stream buffer (don't reuse underlying buffer) or tag chunks with `x-rw-retry-id` to detect concatenation.

tom: alternative: offer NDJSON mode for function outputs (`json_mode: 'ndjson'`) which emits one JSON per line. Clients can then parse line-by-line and it's replay-safe. downside: breaks existing consumers who expect a wrapped payload.

manuel: also consider length-prefix framing for strictness. Easier to robustly parse than brace counting. But it's a server protocol change.

priya: long-term: we should add a cross-sdk parity test: auth-refresh + streaming + function outputs. Matrix: js/py, ndjson/len-prefix/plain-json, retries enabled/disabled. Will file a task.

rachel: immediate plan: Tom will open a tiny patch to js-sdk that adds a `jsonStream.guard()` which buffers up to 128kb and checks brace balance before calling Ajv. If we hit the buffer limit, fallback to validating on final chunk only and log debug + telemetry.

tom: yep, will do. I'll also add a feature-flag `RW_JSONSTREAM_LENPREFIX` so we can dogfood len-prefix in staging without breaking prod. PR will include unit tests mocking mid-stream auth refresh.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: js-sdk/0.12.5-rc (unit: pass, int: running). CI job: #7892.

manuel: i'll add a note to the onboarding sample README explaining the retry edge and recommending `json_mode: 'ndjson'` as a workaround until canary is stable.

priya: let's also add a short blurb to SDK troubleshooting: "If you see JSON schema errors only during retries or auth refreshes, enable the NDJSON or use the stream guard". Saves support tickets.

rachel: thanks all. Tag me on the PR and i'll re-run the sample app against staging once canary finishes.

tom: PR: https://git.redwood/devex/sdk-js/pulls/412 (WIP) — includes brace-guard + tests.

rachel: perfect. filing follow-ups: DEVEX-2145 (parity test), DEVEX-2146 (protocol len-prefix), DEVEX-2147 (docs update).
